title: Structured logging and privacy-aware context guidelines
author: Priya Desai
body:
Summary
-------
This standard describes how services emit structured application logs and how request context may be included without exposing customer or user data. It aims to give us consistent searchable fields, machine-readable logs for alerting and cost analysis, and fewer accidental PII/secret leaks. It covers every service and SDK producing production logs across hosted, dedicated and private deployments.

Why this matters
----------------
- Divergent log schemas slow down incident response and break automated analysis.
- Adding request context without controls raises the chance of PII or secrets landing in telemetry.
- Consistent structure lets alerting, cost attribution and ML ops consumers parse and correlate events reliably.

Scope and ownership
-------------------
- Backend services, edge proxies, workers and ingestion pipelines. Browser/UI logging is covered by the frontend logging guidance.
- Owner: Observability Platform (engineering); steward: Priya Desai.
- Enforcement: CI lint rules, pre-merge checks and runtime sanitizers.

Required fields (JSON log object)
---------------------------------
Each production structured log entry MUST include:
- timestamp (ISO-8601 UTC)
- service (string): registry short name, e.g. "api-gateway"
- env (string): prod, staging, canary or integration
- level (string): DEBUG, INFO, WARN, ERROR or FATAL
- trace_id (string | null)
- request_id (string | null)
- tenant_id (string | null): internal customer id (see tenant redaction rules)
- msg (string): short human-readable message
- event (string): machine event code, e.g. "model.infer.start"
- attrs (object): non-sensitive dimensions only

Example
-------
{"timestamp":"2025-09-22T09:14:05.481Z","service":"embedder","env":"prod","level":"INFO","trace_id":"9c2e...","request_id":"r-71d0","tenant_id":"acct-123","msg":"inference_start","event":"model.infer.start","attrs":{"model":"gptx-8b-q4","seq_len":128,"gpu":"p3.8xlarge"}}

Field guidance
--------------
- timestamp: RFC3339 / ISO-8601 UTC; epoch-only values are not allowed.
- service: names from the service registry (appendix A), without env or role suffixes.
- env: drives retention and alerting tiers downstream.
- level: use semantic levels; do not encode state in the level.
- trace_id/request_id: use OpenTelemetry IDs when available, otherwise null. Never generate ids containing PII.
- tenant_id: internal stable id; external account IDs are mapped to opaque ids at ingest.
- attrs: non-sensitive dimensions only.

Allowed attrs examples
----------------------
- model (short name, no path or key), model_variant, shard
- sequence_length, prompt_tokens, output_tokens (integers)
- gpu_type
- request_cost_microcents (integer)
- rollout_phase (canary|gradual|stable)

Forbidden in logs
-----------------
- Raw user prompts or responses
- API keys, secrets, credentials
- Full email addresses, phone numbers, SSNs or other unredacted identifiers
- File contents, attachments, binary blobs
- Environment variables containing secrets

PII/secrets handling
--------------------
1) Prevention first: never put raw text that could contain PII in attrs or top-level fields.
2) Tokenization: when text context is needed for debugging, log a sha256 hex hash prefixed with "h:" and keep the raw payload in a secured, audited store.
3) Masking: for fields with partial PII (e.g., username), log a redacted value plus fingerprint, e.g. "user.name_redacted":"j****n","user.name_fp":"h:5f4dcc3b5aa765d61d8327deb882cf99"
4) Sampling: textual context for a subset of requests (e.g., failures) must be explicitly sampled—only 0.5% by default in prod, configurable per service with review.
5) Secret detection: pre-commit linters and a runtime filter scan log keys/values for known secret shapes (AWS keys, JWTs); matches fail tests.

Structured vs. unstructured
---------------------------
- Put every dimension used by downstream systems in typed attrs; no free-form "details" strings for machine logic.
- Stack traces and narratives go in a separate "debug" field, escaped and sampled, and excluded from high-retention indexes.

Sampling and retention
----------------------
- Prod defaults: INFO and below are 1% indexed and 100% stored for 7 days in low-cost blob storage; ERROR and above are 100% indexed and retained per SLO (default 30 days).
- High-volume infra services (e.g., ingress proxies) should sample more aggressively.
- Long-running batch jobs should include request_cost_microcents for team cost attribution.

Enforcement
-----------
- Pre-commit lint: required fields, banned keys, attrs types.
- CI contract tests: each service ships a JSON schema (e.g. schema/log-schema.json) and a test validating emitted logs against it.
- Runtime sanitizer at ingestion: enforces max-key-length (128 chars), strips PII-pattern values when sampling is off, and rate-limits oversized log objects.

Schema excerpt
--------------
{"type":"object","required":["timestamp","service","env","level","msg","event","attrs"],"properties":{"timestamp":{"type":"string"},"service":{"type":"string"},"env":{"enum":["prod","staging","canary","integration"]},"level":{"enum":["DEBUG","INFO","WARN","ERROR","FATAL"]},"attrs":{"type":"object"}}}

Libraries
---------
- Use the company logging SDK (github.com/redwood-inference/logging-sdk): JSON formatter with required-field injection, hashing/redaction helpers, sampling decorator and OpenTelemetry integration.
- Python:
  from rdl.logging import get_logger
  logger = get_logger(service="embedder", env="prod")
  logger.info(event="model.infer.start", attrs={"model":"gptx-8b-q4","seq_len":128})
- Go:
  logger := rdl.NewLogger("api-gateway", "prod")
  logger.Info("model.infer.start", rdl.Attrs{"model":"gptx-8b","seq_len":64})

Incident debug workflow
-----------------------
1) From the paged trace id, query logs by trace_id and request_id over the service and time window.
2) If text context was sampled out, request a temporary 10x debug sampling increase for the service (approver and audit log required).
3) Suspected PII in logs: follow the incident-secured procedure (security-and-compliance/incident-response-security).

Migration plan for existing services
------------------------------------
- Phase 1 (2 weeks): adopt the SDK wrapper and add required fields; keep existing keys.
- Phase 2 (4 weeks): add CI schema tests, dry-run for two weeks.
- Phase 3 (2 weeks): enforce linter on main and require green schema tests to merge.
- Phase 4 (ongoing): sanitizer enforced at ingestion; drop unstructured fields after 60 days.

Compliance
----------
- Storage and access follow data-residency and retention policies.
- Access to raw logs that may hold sampled text requires audit approval.

Appendix A: service registry excerpt
------------------------------------
| service | short-name | owner |
|---------|------------|-------|
| API Gateway | api-gateway | infra-team |
| Embedding worker | embedder | ml-serving |
| Model router | model-router | runtime-core |

Appendix B: common failures
---------------------------
- Missing request_id on hot paths: add request-id middleware at the first ingress layer.
- Oversized logs: blocklist large keys at serialization and log a fingerprint.
- Secret detected in CI: open a Security ticket and rotate the key immediately.

FAQ
---
Q: Why not log raw prompts for failed requests?
A: They are high-risk PII and may hold customer secrets; use hashes and the secure payload store.

Q: Who approves increased debug sampling?
A: On-call plus the service owner or delegate; every increase is audited.
